title: Four hospital chains plan 61% more beds
dek: Medanta, Aster DM, Rainbow and Yatharth have announced about 12,200 new beds over three to four years. Most listed chains ran 59–72% full in Q2 FY27; only Max was above 75%.

hero.label: new beds announced by four chains
hero.note: Over three to four years, against about 20,000 they run today. Lists show beds added and the rise on today's base.

read: New beds lose money for two to three years, so FY28–29 margins will rest on how fast chains fill the wards they already have.
sources: Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage analysis

companies.name: Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services Ltd

notes: Bed pipelines are as stated on Q2 FY27 calls: Medanta (Global Health) about 3,450 beds on 3,811 operational; Aster DM 4,230 beds taking its 10,840-bed base past 15,000; Rainbow about 2,300 beds over three years on a ~2,600-bed network; Yatharth's organic target of 5,000 beds in three to four years on ~2,800 operational, excluding 2,000–3,000 beds it plans to acquire. Pipelines are management targets with different horizons, so the total is approximate. Occupancy is as each company states it and bases differ (census vs operational beds; Narayana gives a 60–65% India range, Jupiter an H1 figure for all hospitals). Rainbow is left out of the chart because paediatric hospitals run at a lower ceiling (about 60%); its mature hospitals were around 54%.
